entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Grenfell Tower fire was a devastating conflagration that occurred on 14 June 2017 in the residential tower in North Kensington, London, England, resulting in 72 fatalities and over 70 injuries. The fire was caused by a faulty refrigerator in one of the apartments and rapidly spread throughout the building due to the use of combustible cladding materials. The tragedy led to widespread outrage and calls for improved building safety regulations, with the UK government establishing the Grenfell Tower Inquiry in response.

The Grenfell Tower fire was a stark reminder of the ongoing issue of social housing in the UK, with many residents of the tower living in poverty and relying on local authorities for support. The fire also highlighted the need for greater accountability and transparency in the construction and maintenance of high-rise buildings, with many warning of 'a preventable disaster waiting to happen'.

In the aftermath of the fire, there were numerous calls for greater action to be taken to address the issue of social housing in the UK, with many calling for the creation of new social housing units and improved living conditions for residents of high-rise buildings.

The Grenfell Tower fire will be remembered as a tragic reminder of the need for greater action to be taken to address the issue of social housing in the UK, with many calls for greater accountability and transparency in the construction and maintenance of high-rise buildings.
